A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CLoRA, with matching authors, core methodology, and retained experiments despite the changed title. All 20 pages of v1 and 26 pages of v2, including appendices, provide readable text and visual evidence for comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation comparisons, DINO scores in Table 1, a 50-participant user study, and latent-update/masking ablations in Figure 10.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds CLIP measurements, instance-level evaluation, multi-subject comparisons, and runtime/scalability results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same prompt variants, token-based attention groups, InfoNCE objective, latent updates, and thresholded union masks for fusion. V2 explains style-application modes and same-class token pairing more explicitly, without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds targeted same-class identity separation, multi-person compositions, interacting-object scenes, and selective styling scenarios in Appendices C, D, and G. These substantially extend tested composition requirements. The underlying CustomConcept101/custom-character sources and reported 131-LoRA collection already appear in v1's appendix; they are not newly added coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with OMG, LoRA-Composer, and Orthogonal Adaptation, including Figures 12, 14, and 15 and Table 2. The original Table 1 comparator set remains in Table 1a. LoRACLR is discussed as related work but is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: V2 introduces CLIP-I/CLIP-T metrics, SEEM-based instance evaluation on 700 images per method, 100 compositions with 3–5 input LoRAs and conditioned baselines, H100 resource benchmarking, and a same-seed with/without-box LoRA-Composer comparison. These are new evaluation protocols; the retained SD1.5, 50-step generation setup does not establish a rerun or changed original protocol.

E4.justification: The original latent-update/masking ablation is retained as v2 Figure 6. V2 adds attention-map analysis of style localization, resource scaling with LoRA count, same-class and interaction stress cases, and examinations of bounding-box dependence and OMG failure cases.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates, whereas v2 adds ± quantities throughout the retained DINO/user-study results and new quantitative tables. Both retain ten generation seeds per prompt; additional runs are not established. V2 does not define whether ± represents standard deviation, standard error, or another quantity.

E6.justification: Original DINO and user-study means are retained up to rounding. V2 adds CLIP, instance-level, scalability, and runtime outcomes: Table 3 reports CLoRA average DINO similarity of 57.3%, while Table 2 shows mixed rankings, including average DINO of 0.347 versus Mix-of-Show's 0.351. The book/cup qualitative comparison in v1 Figures 7 and 33 is omitted. New H100 timings do not establish a same-setting speedup over v1.

T1.justification: V2 corrects the background cross-attention definition: text embeddings supply keys/values and UNet features supply queries, reversing v1's query/key assignment. The substantive CLoRA loss, latent-update, and masking equations remain equivalent; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Training-free composition of community LoRAs remains the central contribution. V2 drops the explicit 'first comprehensive attempt' assertion and the conclusion's claim to introduce a DINO-based metric, while making memory efficiency and scalability explicit contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of same-class separation, selective styling, and competitors' dependence on segmentation or supplied controls. It interprets larger compositions as achieving comparable fidelity without auxiliary conditioning and reframes computational scaling as a measured practical tradeoff. V1's explicit limitation that composition depends on input LoRA quality disappears, although ethical concerns remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents 200 prompts, 48 images per user-study participant, randomized presentation, explicit baseline conditioning choices, and detailed H100 runtime/VRAM information. These improve disclosure without establishing changes to retained experiments. Conversely, v1's statement that its main DINO evaluation used six LoRA models is removed.

R1.justification: Related work substantially updates the positioning against OMG, LoRA-Composer, Orthogonal Adaptation, and LoRACLR, emphasizing differences in conditioning, training, segmentation, and community-LoRA compatibility. It also adds bounding-box attention methods and other relevant references while trimming older background citations.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites and condenses the abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological explanation. It changes the title, separates Background from Methodology, folds the ablation discussion into Experiments, and reorganizes supplementary material into Appendices A–J.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the method overview, consolidates v1 Figures 5, 8, and 9 into Figure 5, and restructures the main qualitative comparisons. It adds tables, runtime plots, attention visualizations, and comparison figures. Many retained appendix panels are enlarged from six to two per page, substantially changing visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V1's broad composition claims rely mainly on whole-image DINO scores and qualitative examples. V2 substantially strengthens validation through instance-level evaluation, harder multi-person tests with conditioned baselines, additional similarity metrics, and measured resource scaling. These additions make identity preservation and practical applicability easier to assess. Undefined ± quantities, inconsistent LoRA-Composer memory figures between Table 1b and Appendix F, and removal of the LoRA-quality caveat weaken reporting, but do not outweigh the substantial evaluation gains.
